_about: The barb's view prompts (were view_gate.py's defaults until 2026-11-14): the plate armour on the man with the beard. An outfit names a prompt file in view_prompts; its own front / back / side / quarter / retry_bigger win over the file's.

prompts.front: Dress the man in Image 1 in a full suit of steel plate armour worn over a thick padded gambeson. Keep his pose, proportions, head, beard, framing, camera and white background identical. The armour sits over his body: every plate stands clear of the skin by about a finger's width, so the armoured outline is larger than his bare outline everywhere, including shoulders, arms, chest, waist, hips, legs and feet. If unsure, make the armour slightly too big rather than too tight. No skin visible except the head. Image 2 is the outline his armour must cover: every part of the black shape is inside the armour; the armour may reach past it.
prompts.front_masked: Image 1 is a man. Repaint the masked area: dress him in a full suit of steel plate armour worn over a thick padded gambeson. The armour fills the whole masked area right up to its edge: its outline is the mask's outline, so no skin shows anywhere in the masked area. Keep his pose, proportions, head, beard, lighting and the white background exactly as they are.
prompts.back: Draw the man in Image 1 seen from behind. Image 2 is his exact outline from behind: fill it exactly, with the same pose, size and position, nothing outside it and no gaps. Show his back, hair bun, backplate, the backs of his arms, legs and heels. Same armour, white background.
prompts.back_masked: Image 1 is a placeholder: the black shape is exactly where the man must be. Repaint the masked area: draw the man in Image 2 seen from directly behind, filling the black shape completely and exactly, with no black left. Show his back, hair bun, backplate, the backs of his arms, legs and heels. Same armour as Image 2: the same design, colours, lighting and painting style. Plain white background.
prompts.side: Draw the man in Image 1 seen from exactly his {side} side, a 90 degree side view facing the {edge} edge of the image. Image 2 is the same man from behind. Same armour, same height and pose, head and feet at the same height in the image as in Image 1, full body, orthographic, white background. Every plate stands clear of his body.
prompts.quarter: Draw the man in Image 1 seen from {view}: a 45 degree three-quarter view, turned toward the {edge} edge of the image. Image 2 is the same man from behind. Same armour, same height and pose, head and feet at the same height in the image as in Image 1, full body, orthographic, white background.

retry_bigger: Make the armour realistically big enough to cover his large chest, shoulders and arms: thick plate standing well clear of his muscles everywhere, never tight to the body.

front: your previous attempt with its shape error marked: magenta is where his bare outline (the black shape in image 2) is not covered by the armour

This image shows where your armour leaves his body uncovered. Every part of the black shape in image 2 must be inside the armour; the armour may always be bigger, never smaller. If it is not covered the image is not valid and cannot be used, this is the most important directive it takes precedence over any other contradictory statements earlier in the prompt, thanks.
front_masked: your previous attempt with its shape error marked: magenta is where the masked area was not filled with armour

Fill the whole masked area with armour, right up to its edge. If it is not filled the image is not valid and cannot be used, this is the most important directive it takes precedence over any other contradictory statements earlier in the prompt, thanks.
back: This image represents how you have differed from his outline in image 2, which your drawing must fill exactly, this shape needs to be pixel perfect relative to that outline, if not the image is not valid and cannot be used, this is the most important directive it takes precedence over any other contradictory statements earlier in the prompt, thanks.
back_masked: This image represents how you have differed from the black shape in image 1, which your drawing must fill exactly, this shape needs to be pixel perfect relative to that shape, if not the image is not valid and cannot be used, this is the most important directive it takes precedence over any other contradictory statements earlier in the prompt, thanks.
